name: Floating-drop brine dryer
subtitle: turns desalination brine into dry salt and water

effects.effect: a liquid on a very hot surface floats on a cushion of its own vapour

effect: a liquid on a very hot surface floats on a cushion of its own vapour
how: Every litre of fresh water made from the sea leaves salty brine that is usually dumped back, harming sea life, and boiling it dry fails because salt crusts over the heaters. Here brine is sprayed onto a very hot plate where each drop floats on a cushion of its own steam (Leidenfrost effect), never touching the metal; the drops shrink into balls of salt that roll off, and the steam is condensed into more fresh water.
obstacle: The steam cushion that keeps the plate clean also slows heat into the drops, so it uses more energy per litre than ordinary boilers.
why: Brine dumping is desalination's dirty secret; a crust-free dryer could end it.
real: Searches found Leidenfrost droplet physics and NaCl droplet crystallization studies, and scaling-control ZLD crystallizers, but no Leidenfrost-based brine dryer.
